back: Acts on a sudden idea without thinking first; generally has a negative connotation.
Similar to impetuous, but can be used in a more positive way (e.g., 'impulsive generosity').
Gives an exaggerated expression of pleasure, praise, or gratitude.
Talks too much, especially about unimportant things.
Reserved or says very little; generally has a negative connotation.
Lacks confidence and has a low opinion of oneself.
Unfriendly and not sociable; often used to describe someone who seems distant.
Unfriendly and thinks oneself better than others; disdainful.
Thinks oneself wonderful; self-important (opposite of modest).
Easily deceived or tricked into believing things that may not be true.
Always takes work very seriously and puts in a lot of effort.
Unwilling to change, despite persuasion; a stronger, more negative term is 'pig-headed'.
Lacking in moral principles and prepared to do very bad things.
Easy to be sociable with or start a conversation with.
Prefers not to exaggerate one's own qualities or importance.
